The Bobsled starts here: interrupts off, the stack reset, $083D set to say the menu was loaded over, the BASIC ROM banked out ($01 = $26), the screen blanked in bitmap mode with multicolour on, the CIAs' interrupts off, port A of CIA 1 set to input, black border and background, the video chip's bank 2 ($8000-$BFFF) selected through CIA 2, and the KERNAL's IRQ vector ($0314) at bs_irq. Then the sound engine is copied to where it runs (copy_engine), the raster interrupt set at line 250, and on to bs_main.

Copies ten pages, $9D00-$A6FF, to $C000-$C9FF: the sound engine and the sounds, which run there because the picture's bitmap, unpacked next, covers $A000-$BF3F. The $40 stored in $15 just before is overwritten here before anything reads it.
One byte of the copy, 256 to a page.

The raster interrupt, twice a frame. At line 241 it switches to text mode with the character set at $9800 (the ROM's upper and lower case set, which the video chip sees in this bank) and multicolour off, so the bottom row is text; the next interrupt is at line 251.

At line 251 (250 the first time): bitmap mode and multicolour again for the next frame's picture, the sled's sprites placed (place_sled), a step of the sound engine (sound_step) and the joystick (read_stick); the next interrupt at line 241, and the frame count at $10 for the main loop.
Acknowledges the raster interrupt, restores the registers the KERNAL's handler saved, and returns.

The joystick into $29, its bits turned over so a set bit is a direction held (1 up, 2 down, 4 left, 8 right, $10 fire): port 2 with one joystick ($087D) or for odd-numbered players, port 1 for the others.

Sounds stopped, the event's tune started (sound 0), the first player and attempt; then the main loop, once a frame: by the state in $11, set up a run (bs_setup), run it (bs_run), or after it (bs_after).
An RTS nothing reaches.
After a run. In practice ($081D negative) "PLAY AGAIN?" at column 20 with YES or NO beside it: up chooses YES, down NO, fire confirms.
Fire on the play-again question: YES (the Y at $83E0) sets state 0 for another run; NO falls to the exit.
State 0: the next run is set up on the next frame.

In competition: the next player ($70 counts from 1 to the number of players in $081E, $72 steps through their 32-byte records); after the last, the next attempt ($71), three in all; after the third attempt, back to the menu.
Back to the menu: the stack reset and the loader's $0900, which loads the menu and starts it where it left off.
The question and its two answers for print_bottom, each a column then the text and a zero: "PLAY AGAIN?" at column 20, "YES   " and "NO    " at column 32.
Prints a string on the bottom text row ($83C0): its first byte is the column, then the characters (ASCII, which the ROM's second set shows as capitals) to a zero.
Code nothing reaches: a character's digit value, 0 for a space.

The player's name and country (16 characters from the player's record at $0800 + $72) at the left of the bottom row, spaces to the end of the row, and the player's best time so far (its six characters of text, record offset $10) at column 32 when there is one.
The bitmap address of a multicolour pixel, X across (0 to 159) and Y down: ($1C) = $A000 + (Y AND $F8) times 40 + (X AND $FC) times 2 + (Y AND 7), and the pixel's place in its byte, X AND 3, in $1E.
The bytes before wait_frames decode as LDX #60, its first instruction, which no caller runs: each passes its own count.
Waits X frames.
Waits X frames, then until fire is pressed.
Waits for the interrupt's frame count at $10, then keeps it in $1F for the clock and clears it.
Unpacks each stream in the list at ($16), two bytes an address, to a zero.

Unpacks one stream at ($14), the format of the opening ceremony's pictures: a destination address, then commands of one byte, the top two bits the kind and the low six a count (0 for 64): 0, the next byte repeated; 1, that many bytes copied; 2, that many bytes skipped; 3, that many bytes each followed by two zeros. A zero byte ends it.
The stream's end.
Steps the destination at $12-$13.
Steps the source at $14-$15.

State 0, a run set up: the screen blanked, zero page $10-$6F cleared, the sprites' multicolour and colours, the screen built (build_screen), the clock at 00.00, the far view straight ahead, the sled in the middle of the chute (place 15) and its frame built; the screen on, the course and the map's dots from their starts, one frame and fire, "ATTEMPT" cleared, the runners' sound (6) and a starting speed of $180000.
The sprites' colours for $D025-$D02E: brown and yellow shared by the multicolour sprites, then orange for the even sprites (the outlines, in hires) and yellow for the odd ones (multicolour).
17 zero bytes nothing reads.
Nine spaces at column 20, which clear "ATTEMPT n".

State 1, a frame of the run: the clock, the speed bar, the distance and the course moved on, a piece of the views drawn; then, unless the sled has crashed ($24), the stick, the speed, the bend's push, the sled kept in the chute, the sled's frame and the check of the walls. After a crash, the wreck's slide (crash_step).

Unpacks the picture (bs_picture_list) and prints the player's name; in competition "ATTEMPT" at column 20 and the attempt's digit at column 28. Then the sprites in front of the picture and all eight on, the first sprite buffer ($30) and a dark grey background, which the interrupt's black takes over at once.
"ATTEMPT" at column 20; build_screen puts the digit at column 28.

At most one piece of the screen a frame: the near view when its piece has changed (draw_near), else the far view (draw_far), else the sled's frame (build_sled). Only in a frame with neither view to draw do the runners' sound change and the map's dots go down.
Nothing changed: the runners' sound for the bend (bend_sound) and the map's dots (plot_dots).

The sled at a wall (place 0 or 30) counts frames in $38; ten in a row is a crash: sound 9, the crash flag $24, and the crash's first frame, place 31 on the left wall or 36 on the right. Away from the walls the count is cleared.
Off the walls: the count back to 0.

Each frame after a crash: every five frames the wreck's next frame, places 31 to 35 or 36 to 40; after the last, the sled is no longer placed ($3C and $41 = $FF). Then every three frames the wreck shakes (shake_wreck) and the speed's high byte drops by one; at 0 the run is over: the sounds stopped, the tune, a time of 99.99 recorded (record_time), in competition 30 frames and fire, and state 2. The course goes on moving while the speed lasts, so a wreck that slides over the finish line gets the time on the clock instead (course_step).
The last frame of the crash shown: the sled no longer placed.
The wreck slides to a stop.
Lifts the wreck's sprites 0 to 3 lines from line 103 by the random number, or puts them back on it.
The wreck's sprites at line 103.

The stick, unless the near view's piece is 42 or more (the finish straight, the last seven stretches), when the sled steers itself back to the middle (place 15), one place a frame. Left takes $68/256 of a place a frame, right adds $80/256, and down or fire, with neither held, brakes: $10 off the speed's middle byte a frame while the speed is at least $0B0000.
Left: $68/256 of a place.
Right: $80/256 of a place.
The brake, down or fire.
The finish straight: back to the middle of the chute.

The speed, 24 bits in $31-$33: gravity adds 10 to its middle byte on a straight and 2 in a bend; then friction takes the sled's distance in whole places from its line for the bend (bend_lines) off the middle byte. A speed under $010000 becomes $020202; over $27FFFF it is held there.
The speed's high byte held under $28.
Where in the chute the sled loses nothing, by the bend: place 15, the middle, on a straight; 3, high on the left wall, in a right-hand bend; 27, high on the right wall, in a left-hand one.

The bend's push on the sled. On a straight, with neither left nor right held, the sled drifts to the middle, $20/256 of a place a frame. In a left-hand bend (2) a sled left of the middle is moved one place a frame to it; from the middle out, it is pushed to the right wall by the room left to the wall, doubled as many times as the speed's high byte halves before it reaches 1 (five times at full speed), plus $28, all in 256ths of a place. A right-hand bend (1) does the same to the left wall.
The right-hand bend: the push to the left wall.
The straight: the drift to the middle.
Keeps the sled's place between 0 and 30 (30 and 255/256 at the most).
When the bend changes, and the sled has not crashed, the runners' sound: 6 on a straight, 7 in a bend.
The sled's frame for its place in the chute, from sled_places, into $2D; the place times four into $3E.

From the interrupt: the sled's eight sprites, two by two at the place's X and Y in sled_places, each place a hires outline (the even sprite) over a multicolour sprite (the odd); their shapes from the buffer in $41, the multicolour sprite's the even shape and the outline's the odd. A place past X 255 sets every sprite's high X bit; when adding 24 for the right column carries, only that column's four ($CC).
Puts the top row's sprites at the line in A and the bottom row's 21 lines lower.
The distance, 24 bits in $2E-$30, moved on by the speed's top two bytes.
When the distance's high byte moves on, the course's next stretch: the far view's piece ($3F), the near view's ($40), the bend ($21) and the number of dots for the map ($20). $FF is the finish.
The finish: the sounds stopped, the tune, the time recorded (record_time), in competition 30 frames and fire, and state 2.

Draws far piece $3F into the top of the view, 19 cells across and five down from column 20, row 0, a column at a time: a mask byte for each cell, its set bits standing for the bytes that follow, the clear ones $AA; a zero mask fills the cell with $AA. Piece 16 also turns the colour RAM there light grey (far_grey).
A zero mask: the cell filled with $AA.

Draws near piece $40 into the middle of the view, 12 cells across and seven down from column 23, row 5, a row at a time, over what is there: a mask byte for each cell, its set bits standing for the bytes that follow and its clear ones leaving those bytes as they are; a zero mask leaves the cell alone, unless the next byte is $33, when the byte after fills it.
A zero mask: the cell left alone, or filled when $33 follows.
The colour RAM of the far view's 19 by 5 cells set to light grey.
Steps the course pointer at $36-$37.
Steps the piece pointer at $14-$15.
Plots the stretch's $20 dots of the map's trail, each an X and a Y from ($12): the pixel's two bits set to 3, the colour RAM's colour.
The two bits of each of a byte's four multicolour pixels.
Steps the dot pointer at $12-$13.
The three packed streams of the picture, for unpack_list, and a zero to end: the bitmap ($4EDF), the screen's colours ($5F9A) and the colour RAM's ($6214).

The course: 177 stretches of four bytes, numbered from 0, and $FF at the finish: the far view's piece, the near view's, the bend (0 a straight; 1 a right-hand bend, which throws the sled up the left wall; 2 a left-hand one) and how many of the map's dots to plot. A stretch lasts while the distance's high byte stays the same, 65,536 units: six or seven frames at full speed, eleven at the starting speed. There are eight bends, five to the right (stretches 9, 42, 75, 122 and 154 on) and three to the left (21, 60 and 107 on), and twice the chute runs under a bridge (90 to 98 and 137 to 145). The last seven stretches are the finish straight, under the FINISH banner; the clock stops after the last.
The addresses of the far view's 35 pieces, by number, for draw_far.
The far pieces' addresses' high bytes, read one on from far_pieces.
The addresses of the near view's 49 pieces, by number, for draw_near.
The near pieces' addresses' high bytes, read one on from near_pieces.

The sled across the chute, 41 places of four bytes: the high bit of X, X, Y and the sled's frame. Places 0 to 30 run from high on the left wall (X 215, Y 90) down through the middle (place 15, Y 105) and up the right wall (X 260, Y 90); 31 to 35 are the crash over the left wall and 36 to 40 over the right. place_sled reads the first three bytes and sled_frame the fourth.
A place's X, read one on from sled_places.
A place's Y, read two on.
A place's frame, read three on.
Code nothing reaches: $14-$15 moved on a character cell, eight bytes.
The clock's four digits at 0, and the three bytes after them.

The clock moved on by the frames the main loop waited ($1F), one frame at a time: the frames count to 6, the tenths and seconds to 10, each carry drawing the digit it changes (clock_digit). It stops at 99 seconds, nine tenths and five frames, shown as 99.99: 60 frames to a second, an NTSC machine's.
What each of the clock's digits counts to: 10, 10, 10, and 6 frames to a tenth.
Draws clock digit X, two cells across and two down from clock_font, at its place in clock_places; the frames digit (3) is shown as a hundredths digit from clock_frames.
Where in the bitmap the clock's four digits go: row 19, columns 25, 27, 31 and 33.
The clock places' high bytes, read one on from clock_places.
The hundredths digit shown for each of the six frames of a tenth: 0, 2, 4, 5, 7 and 9.

The bar beside the sled on the panel: three quarters of the speed's high byte, at most 30 pixels, drawn when it changes on three lines, two apart, of eight cells from row 16, column 28: whole cells of $55, then the part cell from bar_ends, then cells of $AA.
The part cell at the bar's end, 0 to 4 pixels of the bar's colour, the bits 01.
The clock's digits 0 to 9, 32 bytes each: the two cells of the top half, then the two of the bottom.

The time into the player's record when it is the player's first or better than the best: the text " ss.hh" at offsets $10-$15, the hundredths from time_frames, and the time turned over at $16-$18 so a better one compares higher.
The new time stored.
The hundredths digits for the record's text, by frame: "024579".

A zero mask: eight zero bytes.
The addresses of the sled's 13 frames, by number, for build_sled.
The frames' addresses' high bytes, read one on from sled_frames.

The sound engine, Hot Dog's, as the file holds it, to $A4A4, with this event's sounds after it to $A689. The start-up (copy_engine) copies $9D00-$A6FF to $C000-$C9FF, where it runs, so every address its code names is $2300 on from the bytes here; the labels here end in _src, and their names without it are where the code runs. First the six slots of 32 bytes (snd_slots), a sound playing in each: +0 the SID voice it plays on (0 to 2), bit 7 set when the slot is idle; +1-2 the script's address; +3 the frames until its next step; +4 a loop count; +5-6 its return stack's pointer; +8 to +14 its copy of the voice's seven registers (frequency, pulse width, control, attack-decay, sustain-release); +15 a flag that restarts the envelope; +16 its transposition; +17 a fine tuning; +18-21 a frequency slide (step, count, rate); +22-25 a pulse-width sweep (step, period, count). The file holds leftover bytes here, which stop_all clears.
Slot 0's script address (+1 and +2), the base start_sound writes each slot's through.
The script address's high byte.
Slot 0's count of frames to its next step (+3).
Slot 0's transposition, tuning, slide and sweep (+16 to +25), which start_sound clears for the slot it starts.
Slots 2 and 3.
Slots 4 and 5.
The slot count of sound_step's loops.
One byte for each SID voice: set once a slot has written the voice this frame, so a slot numbered higher wins a voice over a lower one.
Voice 1's claim.
Voice 2's claim.
Nonzero while the engine runs; start_sound clears it while it writes a slot.
The filter's registers, copied to $D415-$D418 every frame: the cutoff's low and high bytes, the resonance and the voices filtered, the filter mode and the volume.
The cutoff's high byte, for $D416.
The resonance and the voices filtered, for $D417.
The filter mode and the volume, for $D418.
The six slots' return stacks for the scripts' calls, 16 bytes each.
start_sound's copies of X and Y.
start_sound's copy of Y.
Three bytes nothing reads.
The counters of the two arpeggio routines, snd_arp_one and snd_arp_two, which nothing calls.
The second arpeggio routine's counter.
The S key's switch: a press sets it to 1 when it is 0, and clears it, stopping every sound, when it is not. The file holds 1 here, so the first press would stop the sounds.

Starts sound A (100 and above are ignored) from snd_table: its first byte is the slot it plays in, its second the SID voice; the slot's script starts at its third byte on the next step, with the slot's transposition, tuning, slide and sweep cleared. A sound already playing in that slot is cut off.
Steps the slot pointer at $80-$81; nothing calls it.
Steps the script pointer at $82-$83.
Steps the pointer at $86-$87 through a sound's first bytes.
The S key's debounce count, 0 to 2.

The sound engine, once a frame from the interrupt. First the S key, read through CIA 1 (row 1, column 5): pressed after a release, it turns snd_s_key over. The event's start-up makes port A of CIA 1 an input (it writes 0 to $DC02), so the engine's write there drives no row, and the key is seen only when something else pulls row 1 low.
For each of the six slots that is not idle: the frequency slide (snd_slide), the pulse-width sweep, and, when its count of frames runs out, the next step of its script (script_step).
The slide: the rate taken from the count, and the step added to the frequency when it passes zero.

The pulse-width sweep: every frame the step is added to the pulse width, and turned round each time the period runs out. A slip makes it change only the width's low byte: the high byte's add goes to the low byte too, with no INY between.
The slot's frames counted down; at zero its script runs on.

Copies the slots to the SID, from slot 5 down to 0: each voice takes the registers of the highest slot that plays on it, and a slot's restart flag turns the gate off and on again to restart the envelope. Then the filter's four registers.
The SID's three voices' register addresses, $D400, $D407 and $D40E.
The voices' register addresses' high bytes, read one on from sid_voices.
Stops every sound: the slots and their stacks cleared, each slot idle with its stack pointer set, volume 15 with the low-pass mode and nothing filtered, and the SID's voice registers cleared.
The six slots' stack addresses.
Writes 0 to the SID's registers $D400-$D415.
An arpeggio: sets the slot's transposition from the next of 16 steps in snd_arp_table_one. Nothing calls it.
Its 16 transpositions in semitones.
Another, for two slots side by side, from snd_arp_table_two. Nothing calls it either.
Its 16 transpositions.

Runs a slot's script from ($82) until it waits. A byte under $80 is a note: its pitch (set_note), then a byte of how many frames it lasts, and the gate on with the envelope restarted. From $80 a command, its number in the low seven bits, through snd_commands; numbers above 28 stop the sound (cmd_stop).
Steps past a command's last byte and runs the next.
An RTS after snd_continue that nothing reaches.
A note: its pitch, its length, the gate on.
Steps past the length, then sets the restart flag and the gate on.

The 29 commands' routines: 0 set the loop count, 1 loop to an address while the count lasts, 2 start another sound, 3 call machine code, 4 jump to an address, 5 call a part of a script, 6 return from it, 7 end, 8 stop, 9 transpose, 10 tune, 11 jump to machine code, 12 a note with a pulse width, 13 a tied note (no new envelope), 14 the gate off for a time, 15 attack-decay and sustain-release, 16 the waveform and envelope, 17 the pulse width, pulse waveform and envelope, 18 a raw frequency for a time, 19 the slide off, 20 the sweep, 21 the slide, 22 the volume, 23 the resonance, 24 the cutoff, 25 the filter mode, 26 the voices filtered, 27 cutoff, mode and resonance from three bytes, 28 cutoff, resonance and routing, and mode.
The command routines' high bytes, read one on from snd_commands.
Command 11: jumps to the machine code at the next two bytes; its RTS ends the slot's step.
Command 3: calls the machine code at the next two bytes, then goes on with the script.
Jumps through $84-$85.
Back from the machine code to the next command.
Command 7: the slot goes idle.
Command 8, and any number above 28: the slot's registers cleared, the gate left on with no waveform, and two frames later the end command at snd_end_byte.
Command 7 ($87), where cmd_stop points the script.

Sets the slot's frequency from a note byte: the high four bits the octave, the low four the semitone, plus the slot's transposition, from note_freqs shifted right once for each octave under 7; 15 gives the highest frequency, $FFFF, for noise. The slot's fine tuning is added.

The SID frequencies of 24 semitones from C in the top octave: C is $430F, which is 1046.5 Hz on an NTSC machine and two-thirds of a semitone flat on a PAL one, as in the opening ceremony's and the menu's tables.
The frequencies' high bytes, read one on from note_freqs.
Eight bytes of code nothing reaches: a read, a step and a read.
Command 16: the control byte (waveform and gate), attack-decay and sustain-release.
Command 17: the pulse width, then the pulse waveform with the gate ($41), attack-decay and sustain-release.
Command 18: a frequency of two bytes, then a length and the gate on.
A note's length, then the gate on.
Command 4: the script goes on at the next two bytes.
Command 1: the loop count less one; until it reaches 0 the script goes back to the next two bytes' address, then on past them.
Command 0: sets the loop count.
Command 2: starts another sound, often the other voices of a tune.
Command 5: pushes the address after the command onto the slot's stack and goes to the next two bytes' address.
Command 6: back to the address on the slot's stack.
Command 9: the slot's transposition, in semitones.
Command 10: the slot's fine tuning, added to every frequency.
Command 22: the volume, the low four bits of $D418.
Command 24: the filter's cutoff, high byte.
Command 25: the filter mode, the high four bits of $D418.
Command 26: which voices go through the filter, the low four bits of $D417.
Command 23: the resonance, the high four bits of $D417.
Command 27: the cutoff from the first byte and the top bit of the second, the mode from the second's low four bits and the cutoff's low bits from its high four, then the resonance and routing.
Two bytes the filter commands work in.
The filter command's second byte, kept while it works.

Command 21: the slide's rate (255 for every frame) and its step of two bytes, added to the frequency at that rate: the rate is taken from a count each frame, and each time the count passes zero the step is added.
Command 20: the sweep's period and its step.
A note command no table entry reaches: pitch, length, gate.
Command 13: a new pitch and length with no new envelope, the notes tied.
A pulse-width command no table entry reaches.
Command 15: attack-decay and sustain-release.
Command 14: the gate off, and a wait of the next byte's frames.
Command 12: a note with the pulse width's high byte, then its length.
Command 19: the slide stopped.
Command 28: the cutoff's high byte, the resonance and routing, and the mode.
The addresses of the event's 31 sounds, by number, for start_sound, where they run. Each sound is a slot, a SID voice and a script. Numbers 1 to 5 and 10 to 26 point to one that does nothing.
The sounds' addresses' high bytes, read one on from snd_table.

The random number at random_seed, 24 bits with the high byte first, shifted right once, the bit fed in at the top the exclusive or of the low byte's bits 0 and 5. The wreck's shake and the runners' rumble step it.
The random number's three bytes, $7F each in the file.
The random number's middle byte, whose low bits shake_wreck reads.
Its low byte, whose bits 0 and 5 make the next bit.
Sound 8, the runners on the ice, under sounds 6 and 7: a quiet triangle on voice 1 (slot 1), nine semitones up, sliding down, which then jumps to rumble_step on every step.
The jump back to the machine code, so rumble_step runs each time the slot steps.

The rumble's machine code: a random note of eight, C to G in the engine's octave 3, which the slot's transposition raises nine semitones (set_note), then a random length of 1 to 8 stored through ($F0) at offset 3. The engine keeps its slot pointer at $80, not $F0, so the length never reaches the slot, whose count stays at 1: the note changes every frame. $F0-$F1 are the KERNAL's line links for the bottom two rows of the screen, $87 and $87 here, so the byte lands at $878A, inside far_panorama: a few pixels of sky in far pieces 21 to 25 change at random as the run goes on. Then the script pointer is stepped past the jump's address.
The sound for the unused numbers: slot 0, voice 2, and an immediate stop.
Sound 7, in a bend: the rumble (sound 8), then noise on voice 0 rising for 32 frames, then a high noise held.
The bend's noise held, a tie of 255 frames over and over.
Sound 6, on a straight and at the start: the rumble, then noise on voice 0 falling for 34 frames, then a lower noise held.
The straight's noise held, a tie of 255 frames over and over.
The bass's figure, 15 notes of 9 frames and a rest of 9, 144 frames: G, D, the D an octave up, G, C, B, G and the G an octave up, then the first seven again.

Sound 0, the tune, before each run and after it: the bass on voice 0, a pulse wave, which starts the two voices above (sounds 29 and 30), then plays the figure three times, once from F (F, C, the C an octave up, F, B, A, G and D, then the first seven again), and the figure again. It goes round from the three figures, 720 frames, until the sounds are stopped.
Where the bass goes round again.

Sound 29, the melody on voice 1, a sawtooth: after 126 frames' rest, B, C and a long D; B, C, D, C and a long B; B, D, C, A, F, C and a long D; a rest of 432 frames; then a long F, F again sliding a little and a long G. Round again every 1,440 frames.
Where the melody goes round again.
Sound 30, the harmony on voice 2, a sawtooth tuned a little sharp: the melody's rhythm a third below, G, A and B; G, A, B, A and G; G, B, A, F, C, A and B; then C, C and D.
Where the harmony goes round again.
Sound 27, under the crash: a long burst of noise on voice 0, sinking for 127 frames.

Sound 28, under the crash: a triangle on voice 2 that whistles up fast for 106 frames, which cannot be heard. Its mode command sets bit 7 of $D418, which takes voice 2 (the SID's third) out of the output unless the filter routes it, and its route command leaves it unfiltered; the bit stays set until the sounds are stopped.
Sound 9, the crash: sounds 27 and 28, then a triangle on voice 1 falling for 12 frames and a lower one sinking for 74.
The file's last 117 bytes, after the sounds, which nothing reads: the leftover fill of $FF, $FE, $01 and $00.

The fast loader's start, run once at power-on. Silences the SID (loader_sid), copies the loader to $0900-$0DFF and clears $0800-$08FF for the variables every part shares, shortens the unused block receiver's delays on a PAL machine ($02A6 = 1), starts the drive code (loader_start_drive), sets $083D (the menu must be loaded) and two joysticks ($087D), points the NMI vector at ldr_nmi and the STOP vector at ldr_stop_never, keeps the IRQ vectors, parks the sprites, stops Shift and Commodore from switching the font, reads the world records into $0E00, then loads and runs the title (file 3) with $0900 pointed at $C0DC, so that the title's exit loads and runs the opening ceremony (file 1).

The 25 values loader_boot writes to SID registers $D400-$D418: each voice at frequency $0F0F, pulse width $0F0F, noise with the gate on ($81), attack and decay $0F, sustain and release $0F; filter 0 and volume 0, so nothing is heard.

Opens the drive's buffer channel ("#", channel 2) and its command channel with "B-E 2 0 18 5", which makes the drive run the code in track 18 sector 5 from buffer 0, then waits for the drive code to answer on the serial bus.
Opens the drive's command channel 15 with "B-E 2 0 18 5" (12 characters at str_block_execute), which starts the drive code.
OPEN 2,8,2,"#": a channel to a buffer in the drive, for the B-E command to load the code into.
"B-E 2 0 18 5", the DOS command that loads track 18 sector 5 into the drive's buffer on channel 2 and runs it; then "#", the buffer channel's name.

The loader as the file holds it, which loader_boot copies to $0900-$0DFF: the same bytes as $0900-$0DEC, but for those the game changes after the copy ($0B08, $0B96 and the PAL patch at $0C66-$0CC1). It stays here unused after the copy, since nothing loads over $C000.
The loader's source for $0A00-$0AFF (loader_copy_src's second page).
The rest of the source for $0A00-$0AFF, $0A40-$0AFF.
The loader's source for $0B00-$0BFF.
The rest of the source for $0B00-$0BFF, $0B40-$0BFF.
The loader's source for $0C00-$0CFF, the PAL-patched part of it before the patch.
The rest of the source for $0C00-$0CFF, $0C40-$0CFF.
The second part of the loader's source copy (loader_copy_src), $0D00-$0DEC at their own addresses; the file ends at $C636.
